long.title: Amazon's Nuclear Bet and 4 More Tech Stories
long.pinned_comment: Which of these five developments will have the biggest impact over the next five years?

intro.text: Artificial intelligence is hungry for power, and tech companies are reviving dead coal plants with nuclear reactors.
That is just one of five major stories shaping the technology landscape right now.
From a massive equity promise by Elon Musk to a surprise ban on federal AI systems, let us count down the top stories you need to know.

scenes.text: Artificial intelligence has just crossed a massive threshold by tackling a 160-year-old math problem.
OpenAI announced that its systems claimed to settle a weaker version of the famous Riemann hypothesis.
Jared Duker Lichtman of Stanford University called it the most significant AI-for-math achievement so far by quite a margin.
Resolving the core hypothesis would help researchers better understand the nature of prime numbers.
Surprisingly, the proof did not need new concepts, but instead unearthed hidden connections between old ones.
According to Maksym Radziwiłł of New York University, most consequences of the main hypothesis already follow from this result.
Number theorists are now working to understand the proof and figure out what this milestone means for mathematics.
The United States government has ordered civilian federal agencies to strip DeepSeek out of their computers.
The order was signed by Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin under a 2018 supply chain law.
Agencies must immediately stop buying products from the Chinese lab and its affiliates.
Crucially, the ban also covers third-party products and services developed using DeepSeek implementations.
The Department of Homeland Security cites multiple threat vectors, including servers located in China.
This rule applies across civilian executive branch agencies, excluding military and intelligence systems.
The order applies to federal civilian executive branch agencies except for their national security systems.
Apple has sent out invites for a product event on October 28th in Los Angeles.
Bloomberg reports that the headline announcement will be a new MacBook Pro featuring an OLED touchscreen.
The new laptop is also expected to be lighter and include an iPhone-like Dynamic Island.
Apple is additionally planning to reveal a 14-inch MacBook Pro and an updated iPad Mini.
Elon Musk says he plans to give one of his SpaceX shares to every child in the US.
With about 72 million children in the country, that gift would be worth roughly 10.5 billion dollars, according to CNBC.
Musk appears to be giving away the shares through Trump Accounts, which are tax-advantaged investment accounts.
This follows major contributions to the accounts from other tech leaders, including six point two five billion dollars from Dell's founder.
Musk stated on social media that this giveaway will be the first of many.
The announcement came shortly after AI company Anthropic pledged five percent of its shares to a public benefit fund.
Amazon has signed an agreement to fund a new nuclear energy facility at a former coal plant in Indiana.
The facility will replace the defunct Breed Generating Station in Sullivan County.
The proposed plant aims to provide up to 960 megawatts of carbon-free energy.
That power will feed both the regional power grid and Amazon's growing data centers.
The project targets twelve advanced small modular reactors developed by X-energy.
These reactors can use air or water cooling, allowing deployment in water-constrained regions.
This is Amazon's second nuclear collaboration, with a goal of deploying over 5 gigawatts by 2039.
Meta, Microsoft, and Google are also exploring nuclear projects to feed their AI infrastructure.
